motion: The government should raise the retirement age.

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: Why should government raise the retirement age instead of ensuring that employers offer decent pensions and that public funds are collected fairly from those able to pay?

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Welcome. Tonight's motion is that the government should raise the retirement age. Paula supports it, and Mira opposes it. Each has thirty seconds for an opening, followed by two and a half minutes of crossfire, then thirty-second closings. I will give a ten-second cue. Keep remarks direct, listen closely, and address the motion.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: People live longer and many can work longer, so retirement rules should reflect that change. A gradual higher age keeps experienced workers contributing and eases pressure on public pensions. It should include fair support for people in demanding jobs. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Okay, Paula, thank you Mira.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: A higher retirement age treats unequal lives as if they were identical. Many people reach later life worn down by physical work, caregiving, or poor health. Government should protect a reliable exit from work, not postpone it for everyone. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: And now we move on to round two. Round two is where the debaters address each other. You get two and a half minutes from the moment I finish speaking. I will give you a ten-second warning.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: No, a general increase is not fair merely because some people can work longer. Your support for exceptions proves the rule would burden people least able to continue working.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Workplaces also need better training and safer conditions, which matter at every age. But the central issue is retirement: a gradual rise, with protections, matches longer working lives.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Your word "gradual" is the weak point. A slow unfair change still forces a tired worker to wait, while protections are promises that can be narrowed later.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: If the retirement age never changes while people spend more years after work, how will you preserve pension support without asking fewer workers to carry more responsibility?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Consider a warehouse worker whose knees fail near retirement. Raising the age means pain, lost wages, or a difficult claim for help; that proves one rule can punish workers-

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: That example supports tailored protection, not freezing the age for everyone. A worker able to continue should have a retirement system that recognizes longer lives and shared responsibilities.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: And tailored protection creates endless arguments at workplaces about whose pain counts and who must prove it. Supervisors may pressure older workers to disclose private limits, leaving dignity dependent on office judgments.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Come back to the whether the government should raise the retirement age, will you?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: On whether government should raise the retirement age, no: individualized hardship cannot repair a blanket delay. The rule shifts risk onto workers while making retirement less certain.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: You call it a blanket delay, but I proposed a gradual change with protections. Rejecting any adjustment ignores the real problem of sustaining retirement promises over longer lives.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Why should a person who began exhausting work early be required to wait longer simply because another person had a comfortable career and can keep working?

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: A caregiver nearing retirement may choose part-time work for a few more years, keeping skills and income while pension costs stay manageable. That proves a flexible higher age can expand options.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Your caregiver example misses the point: choice is not protection when bills force the choice. A higher age turns voluntary extra work into a delayed guarantee.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: No, bills need not force anyone if protections are designed properly. Why deny capable older workers a system that remains stable enough to support every generation?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I agree that pension systems need careful planning. But the main answer is fair funding, not making workers wait longer; retirement should remain a dependable right.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Ten seconds, both of you.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: "Fair funding" is too vague to solve the pressure you admit exists. Without adjusting retirement-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: That's time. And now we move on to round three. And those will be closing statements by each debater. And speaking first and answering yes to whether the government should raise the retirement age, here again, is Paula.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: A retirement system must endure, not simply promise benefits it cannot reliably maintain. Raising the age gradually recognizes longer lives while protecting workers who genuinely cannot continue.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: But your protection is only a slogan when a worker-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Please let her address the principle.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: -while protecting workers who genuinely cannot continue. The principle is shared responsibility: those able to work longer help preserve secure pensions for those who cannot.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Ten seconds.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Raise the age gradually, protect hardship, and keep retirement secure for everyone. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Please, Mira. That's where I was going next.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: This motion asks government to make a basic guarantee harder to reach. Longer lives do not mean equally healthy lives or equally easy jobs. Paula offers exceptions, but workers should not need to prove they are worn down before receiving retirement. A fair system funds its promise rather than moving the finish line. Government should strengthen retirement security, not raise the retirement age.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Ten seconds for last word.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Even a gradual increase leaves the least powerful workers carrying the greatest risk. People who can continue may do so voluntarily, but everyone-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Time out. Time out.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Thank you, Paula and Mira, for a focused debate. That concludes our discussion of this motion.
